The claim by the Petitioner as per the Arbitration Award dated 9.9.2000, passed by the Arbitral Tribunal comprising the Sole Arbitrator Sh. Thakar Das in favour of the M/s Karam Chand Thapar & Bros(CS) Ltd. Vide the said award, the Petitioner was directed to make payment of Rs. 194.33 lakh with interest @ 21% from 2.11.1992 till the date of payment in favour of contractor, namely, M/s Karam Chand Thapar & Bros (CS) Ltd in relation to the work under the “Tail Race Tunnel-II outlet package” of the generating station. 146. The Petitioner had challenged the said order before the Hon’ble Delhi High Court, wherein a Single Bench vide its order dated 11.2.2010 set aside the arbitration award passed in favour of the contractor. The order dated 11.2.2010 was subsequently set aside by the Division Bench of the Hon’ble Delhi Court, vide its order dated 16.5.2024, thereby upholding the award of the Arbitral Tribunal. 150. The Respondent, PSPCL, in its reply, has disputed the said cost and has submitted that the claims sought by the Petitioner under Regulation 91 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations cannot be allowed, as no details have been furnished by the Petitioner with respect to the segregation of interest component, year-wise impact, or actual payment records. The Respondents BRPL, BYPL and RUVNL, in their reply, have objected to the interest amount claimed by the Petitioner and have submitted that the said claim of the Petitioner be rejected since the Petitioner has failed to take any prudent steps to stop this exorbitant liability for almost 24 years at the rate of 21%. 151. The Petitioner, in its rejoinders to the replies, has submitted that there is no delay in payment as the award was complied with promptly upon conclusion of the judicial process and receipt of court directions permitting the deposit of the amount. The accrual of interest was a direct consequence of prolonged judicial proceedings, which the Petitioner contested in good faith at every forum to minimise the impact on beneficiaries. 162. The Respondent, PSPCL, in its reply, has stated that the reimbursement of interest paid by the Petitioner on 15.1.2020 (against the 75% payout of the arbitral award) is not supported under Regulation 91 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, as notional interest is not a reimbursable component unless specifically allowed under the regulations. PSPCL has also highlighted the apprehension with regard to prematurely dealing with the above-stated claim during the pendency of the arbitration before the Hon’ble Delhi. The Respondents, BYPL and RUVNL, in their replies, have stated that the payment was made by the Petitioner on 15.1.2020, the 2024 Tariff Regulations have been made applicable by the Commission w.e.f. 1.4.2024, in this regard, both BYPL and RUVNL have prayed for rejection of the claim of the Petitioner since the same lacks regulatory sanctity and falls out of the control period of 2024 Tariff Regulations. Also, the Respondent, BRPL, in its reply, has highlighted that a huge amount of interest has been paid due to mismanagement on the part of the Petitioner, which should not be passed on to the beneficiaries.
